questions.q: Who came to Ezekiel to inquire of him?
questions.a: The elders of Israel came to Ezekiel to inquire of him.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh question if he should be inquired of by these men?
questions.a: Yahweh questioned because the elders had taken their idols into their hearts.

questions.q: How did Yahweh say he would answer those who take idols into their hearts?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would answer those who take idols into their hearts according to the number of their idols.

questions.q: What did Yahweh call the house of Israel to do?
questions.a: Yahweh called the house of Israel to repent and turn away from its idols.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do to every man who worships idols and then seeks to inquire from a prophet of Yahweh?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would make that man a sign and a proverb by cutting him off from the people of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do to every deceived prophet?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would deceive that prophet and destroy him.

questions.q: What relationship did Yahweh say he wanted with the people of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh said he wanted the people to be his people, and for him to be their God.

questions.q: When Yahweh brought judgment, what would be all that even the most righteous in the land could do?
questions.a: When Yahweh brought judgment, even the most righteous in the land could only deliver their own souls.

questions.q: Who did Yahweh use as examples of some of the most righteous men in history?
questions.a: Yahweh used as examples of some of the most righteous men in history Noah, Daniel, and Job.

questions.q: Who did Yahweh use as examples of some of the most righteous men in history?
questions.a: Yahweh used as examples of some of the most righteous men in history Noah, Daniel, and Job.

questions.q: When Yahweh brought judgment, who would the most righteous in the land not be able to deliver?
questions.a: When Yahweh brought judgment, the most righteous in the land would not be able to deliver their sons or daughters.

questions.q: What four punishments did Yahweh say he would send to Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would send the four punishments of famine, sword, wild animals, and plague.

questions.q: After Yahweh’s judgment, who would be left?
questions.a: After Yahweh’s judgment, a remnant would be left who would go out with sons and daughters.

questions.q: What would cause Ezekiel to be comforted?
questions.a: When Ezekiel saw the ways and actions of the remnant of survivors, he would be comforted.

commentary.text: Threatenings against hypocrites. (Ezek. 14:1-11) God's purpose to punish the guilty Jews, but a few should be saved. (Ezek. 14:12-23)

Ezek. 14:1-11 No outward form or reformation can be acceptable to God, so long as any idol possesses the heart; yet how many prefer their own devices and their own righteousness, to the way of salvation! Men's corruptions are idols in their hearts, and are of their own setting up; God will let them take their course. Sin renders the sinner odious in the eyes of the pure and holy God; and in his own eyes also, whenever conscience is awakened. Let us seek to be cleansed from the guilt and pollution of sins, in that fountain which the Lord has opened.

Ezek. 14:12-23 National sins bring national judgments. Though sinners escape one judgment, another is waiting for them. When God's professing people rebel against him, they may justly expect all his judgments. The faith, obedience, and prayers of Noah prevailed to the saving of his house, but not of the old world. Job's sacrifice and prayer in behalf of his friends were accepted, and Daniel had prevailed for the saving his companions and the wise men of Babylon. But a people that had filled the measure of their sins, was not to expect to escape for the sake of any righteous men living among them; not even of the most eminent saints, who could be accepted in their own case only through the sufferings and righteousness of Christ. Yet even when God makes the greatest desolations by his judgments, he saves some to be monuments of his mercy. In firm belief that we shall approve the whole of God's dealings with ourselves, and with all mankind, let us silence all rebellious murmurs and objections.
